A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SPARC research. Their main text, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching of retained, relocated, and added content.

before.justification: V1 reports original Qwen3-VL and Molmo2 benchmark evaluations, crop-localization experiments, perceptual-consistency studies, and fine-tuning results.

after.justification: V3 retains those original results and adds controlled comparisons, robustness tests, latency measurements, and broader model and task evaluations.

M1.justification: Appendix A.5 adds a bottom-up SPARC variant: partition the image into a 3 × 3 grid, run IRD independently on each tile, map predictions to global coordinates, and apply WBF. The standard two-stage pipeline, perceptual fusion, and perception-only LoRA activation remain unchanged.

E1.justification: V3 adds GQA Global for whole-scene questions and MME Realworld for perception and reasoning across autonomous driving, diagrams/tables, monitoring, OCR, and remote sensing. It also evaluates distant-object spatial queries separately. The original V*, HRBench, XLRS, and DeepEyes coverage is retained.

E2.justification: V3 adds substantive controlled comparators: bottom-up grid-based SPARC in Table 5, raw unfused IRD rollouts against WBF in Table 6, and end-to-end reasoning-trace Distillation SFT in Table 10. The original native-model, thinking-with-images, and literature comparator sets remain.

E3.justification: Added protocols extend rollout testing to 64, introduce localization-area and coverage diagnostics, and measure TTFT and end-to-end latency. V3 also evaluates SPARC with the 235B-A22B model and specifies filtered robustness samples of 16 V* and 157 GQA questions. These extend evaluation; the original resolution and training settings are retained.

E4.justification: New analyses test top-down versus grid-based search, whether WBF preserves accuracy while removing redundant crops, saturation beyond eight rollouts, vulnerability to global or distant-object queries, and decoupled versus full-trace training. These address component effectiveness and failure conditions beyond v1's existing crop, resolution, and qualitative analyses.

E5.justification: V3 introduces no new seed reporting, repeated-run uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Increasing IRD rollout counts changes inference computation, not statistical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: The original numerical tables are retained, while substantial new results appear in Tables 5–8 and 10–12. Examples include WBF accuracy saturation, distillation-baseline degradation, measured latency, and 91.6% V* accuracy for 235B SPARC. MME results are mixed: at 256 resolution, the 8B model scores 26.1 with SPARC versus 28.7 natively. These are added comparisons, not revisions to retained scores.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theorems or proofs. The existing conceptual account of IRD and perception–reasoning separation is retained; the new empirical diagnostics introduce no substantive mathematical derivation or formal property.

C1.justification: The abstract's headline gains and the three introductory contributions remain unchanged. The revised conclusion makes a more categorical claim that SPARC prevents perceptual errors from cascading into hallucinations, modestly strengthening v1's claim of robust and efficient inference.

C2.justification: V3 adds explanations of WBF saturation, grid-search trade-offs, preservation of global context, and degradation from full-trace distillation. It newly states the native-grounding requirement and implementation dependence of latency. Some interpretations exceed the evidence: the general-reasoning 'no penalty' claim overlooks regressions in Table 12.

D1.justification: Appendix A.13 specifies the previously described off-the-shelf thinking-with-images decoding parameters. New experiments document the vLLM latency backend, grid/subset construction, and matched-recipe distillation setup. Existing prompts, LoRA hyperparameters, training hardware, and training-time disclosures are retained or relocated rather than newly introduced.

R1.justification: V3 adds references on overthinking, visual blindness, bias and mirage reasoning, plus GQA, MME Realworld, and vLLM. It also explicitly relates SPARC to bottom-up divide-and-conquer approaches. The principal neuroscience and context-engineering positioning remains; many other citation changes simply update publication metadata or attribution.

P1.justification: V3 copyedits the abstract and main text, rewrites the conclusion, adds acknowledgements, corrects the running header, and reorganizes appendix sections. The main narrative and section sequence remain substantially intact; most expansion accompanies new scientific content rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: V3 adds substantial comparative displays in Tables 5–8 and 10–12, including rollout diagnostics, latency comparisons, and the multidomain MME table. Existing appendix tables are relocated and renumbered, with associated layout changes. Figures 1–9 retain their graphical content.

improvement.justification: V1 lacked direct raw-crop and full-trace training controls and measured latency evidence. V3 supplies these, making the benefits of fusion and decoupled training substantially more assessable, while testing broader applicability and stating a grounding limitation. The new no-penalty interpretation overlooks MME regressions, and the largest latency factors compare different resolutions. These qualifications constrain the claims but do not erase the substantial improvement in evidence for the central framework.
